subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Should expected non-zero command outcomes use a new explicit result contract, or should OpenClaw intentionally stop warning for every normally terminated non-zero exec result?
rationale: The runtime's existing `completed` status cannot distinguish benign command-specific outcomes from genuine failures, so choosing the permanent warning semantics requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit expected-exit semantics
options.body: Keep generic non-zero exits as failures and suppress warnings only when the execution layer explicitly marks that outcome as expected.

options.title: Suppress all normal non-zero exits
options.body: Accept that any process reaching a normal exit will not trigger a channel warning, including ordinary command failures.

recommendation.title: Add explicit expected-exit semantics
recommendation.body: Keep generic non-zero exits as failures and suppress warnings only when the execution layer explicitly marks that outcome as expected.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work owns the shared tool-error warning and agent message-filtering path where this semantic decision becomes user-visible.
